watchForNext.neutral: You might notice longer stretches of deep focus, half an hour or more on a build or a book, when something has really caught them. Watch too for them managing their own attention, like moving somewhere quieter or asking a sibling to wait.

variants.charlotte_mason: Within short, focused lessons, watch for full attention holding steady even when the work gets hard, and for the child noticing a wandering mind and bringing it back.
variants.classical: Watch for a full lesson worked through with steady focus, including the harder parts, and for the child setting up their own space to work without distractions.
variants.montessori: Watch for long, uninterrupted work cycles in which the child chooses the work and stays with it, and for them protecting their own concentration.
variants.waldorf_steiner: Within the rhythm of the main lesson, watch for absorption deepening during painting, handwork or a story, and for a calm return to the task after a break.
variants.unschooling: Look for long stretches of absorbed play or project work, an hour lost in building or drawing, and for the learner arranging their own space to keep going.
variants.eclectic: Whether at the table or on the floor with a build, watch for longer stretches of focus, and for the child setting up their own space to keep going.

watchForNext.neutral: You might hear connections across subjects, like 'that's like the pyramids we read about' while building a sandcastle. Watch too for little memory tricks of their own, such as a rhyme or a made-up song to remember something.

variants.charlotte_mason: In narrations, listen for ideas from one book appearing in another, and for things learned weeks ago drawn on without a reminder.
variants.classical: As memory work grows, listen for chants, facts and poems pulled out at just the right moment, and for the child inventing rhymes of their own to remember new facts.
variants.montessori: Watch for something learned with one material applied to new work, and for spontaneous connections between different areas of the environment.
variants.waldorf_steiner: As each main lesson block is recalled in the days and weeks after, listen for the child linking what was learned to a new story, season or activity.
variants.unschooling: Look for knowledge from different interests colliding, a fact from a documentary popping up during a game, or a trick from one project used in another.
variants.eclectic: Watch for connections made across subjects, and for memory tricks of their own, like rhymes or songs.

watchForNext.neutral: You might notice a problem appearing in their stories, like the dragon stealing the cake, and then a way it gets solved. Watch too for characters with their own personalities, and for the same story told with toys, drawings and words.

variants.charlotte_mason: In narration and play, watch for invented stories taking shape around a problem to solve, and for characters from living books given new adventures.
variants.classical: Watch for stories told in clear order, beginning, middle and end, with a problem and a solution, and for familiar stories retold with a new ending.
variants.montessori: Watch for stories told about real life, and for small figures or drawings used to plan out what happens next.
variants.waldorf_steiner: Imaginative play is central here. Watch for play-stories with a problem and a solution, often echoing fairy tales, and for characters who return day after day.
variants.unschooling: Look for long-running imaginary worlds in play, characters who return, plots that build over days, and stories acted out with toys or friends.
variants.eclectic: Whether told aloud, drawn or played out with toys, watch for stories with a problem and a solution, and for characters with personalities of their own.

watchForNext.neutral: You might hear them counting the corners and sides of shapes, and naming solid shapes like cubes, cones and cylinders in the pantry or the toy box. Watch too for a triangle recognised even when it's upside down.

variants.charlotte_mason: On walks and at home, watch for shapes spotted in nature and buildings, and for the child describing how they are the same and how they differ.
variants.classical: As shape names are learned, watch for a shape's properties listed, its sides and corners, and for the shape recognised in any position.
variants.montessori: After the geometric cabinet and the geometric solids, watch for shapes and solids named in the world around them, and for their edges traced with interest.
variants.waldorf_steiner: Through form drawing and movement, watch for shapes walked, drawn and sensed, and for delight in finding a circle, a triangle or a spiral in nature.
variants.unschooling: Look for shapes turning up in building, packing and play, a cylinder chosen as a tower base, or a cube-shaped box noticed to fit the cupboard better.
variants.eclectic: Watch for corners and sides counted, solid shapes named, and shapes recognised whichever way they're turned.

watchForNext.neutral: You might see them working out what a box looks like flattened out, or picturing how a shape will look turned around before they try it. Watch too for shapes grouped with a reason, like 'these all have a square face'.

variants.charlotte_mason: In handicrafts and drawing, watch for the child picturing how a flat shape will fold into a box, and explaining why certain shapes belong together.
variants.classical: Watch for shapes classified by their properties with clear reasons, and for angles described as bigger or smaller than a square corner.
variants.montessori: After work with the constructive triangles and geometric solids, watch for nets of solids folded by the child, and for noticing how shapes combine to make others.
variants.waldorf_steiner: Watch for mirror-symmetry form drawings becoming more confident, and for shapes imagined turning and folding in the mind's eye.
variants.unschooling: Look for spatial puzzles in their play: building something from a picture, folding paper planes, designing a symmetrical build, or finding the way with a map.
variants.eclectic: Whether with paper nets or building bricks, watch for shapes pictured turning in the mind, and for shapes grouped by their properties.

watchForNext.neutral: You might hear them asking their own counting questions, like 'what's everyone's favourite fruit?', and keeping track with tally marks. Watch too for a simple chart or picture graph made to show what they found.

variants.charlotte_mason: On nature walks, watch for finds counted and recorded, birds seen or flowers by colour, and for totals compared from week to week.
variants.classical: Watch for answers to a question collected and tallied, and for the results shown in a simple chart with labelled columns.
variants.montessori: Watch for sorting work turning into counting and recording, with a chart made of the child's own collection and the biggest group pointed out.
variants.waldorf_steiner: Watch for counting and comparing woven into the seasons, how many flowers in the garden this week or birds at the feeder, recorded in pictures.
variants.unschooling: Look for surveys and tallies of the learner's own making: favourite colours in the family, cars passing the window, wins in a card game.
variants.eclectic: Watch for questions they want to answer by counting, tally marks to keep track, and a simple chart to show what they found.

watchForNext.neutral: You might see the tablet used to make something rather than watch something, such as a short stop-motion film, a slideshow or a drawing with layers. Watch too for step-by-step instructions given to a person or a toy robot, and for a step fixed when it goes wrong.

variants.charlotte_mason: Where screens are used sparingly, watch for the camera or a drawing app used to record nature finds and handicrafts, and for clear step-by-step instructions given aloud.
variants.classical: Watch for precise step-by-step instructions written or spoken by the child, and for simple digital projects carried through in order from plan to finished piece.
variants.montessori: Watch for technology used as a tool for the child's own work, photographing a project or making a simple slideshow, and for steps sequenced with cards before any screen.
variants.waldorf_steiner: Screens are usually kept for later here. Watch instead for the thinking behind them: steps sequenced in a craft, precise instructions given and followed, and a mistake in the sequence found.
variants.unschooling: Look for the learner making things with technology, a stop-motion film with toys, a game level, a photo story, and working out what went wrong when it doesn't work.
variants.eclectic: Watch for devices used to create rather than just watch, and for step-by-step instructions that get fixed when they go wrong.

watchForNext.neutral: You might notice family screen rules followed without a reminder, and the device put down when the agreed time is up. Watch too for them coming to tell you when something online feels strange or uncomfortable.

variants.charlotte_mason: Watch for habits of self-control around screens forming, the device set aside when time is up, and for the child telling you about anything that felt wrong.
variants.classical: As family rules for devices are learned and discussed, watch for them followed independently, and for the child explaining why a rule exists.
variants.montessori: Watch for the child taking responsibility for their own device use within clear limits, and coming to an adult when something doesn't feel right.
variants.waldorf_steiner: Where devices are introduced, watch for agreed limits kept without a reminder, and for the child telling you when something they saw felt wrong.
variants.unschooling: Look for limits the learner sets with you and then keeps, and for open talk about what they've seen online, the good and the strange.
variants.eclectic: Watch for family device rules kept without reminders, and for the child coming to tell you when something online feels wrong.

watchForNext.neutral: You might see a little planning before writing, like a list of ideas or a quick sketch of the story's parts. Watch too for writing shaped for a reader, like a joke saved for the end, or a sentence changed because 'it sounds better this way'.

variants.charlotte_mason: Oral narration stays at the heart of composition here. Listen for narrations that are longer, better ordered and richer in words, and watch for the first short written narrations.
variants.classical: Watch for written narrations and short compositions planned with a simple outline, and for sentences revised so they don't all start the same way.
variants.montessori: Watch for longer pieces written about the child's own research or experiences, and for drafts revised after reading them aloud to someone.
variants.waldorf_steiner: Watch for the child's own compositions appearing in the main lesson book, retellings and descriptions, written with care for how they sound when read aloud.
variants.unschooling: Look for writing with a real reader in mind, a letter to a pen pal, a comic for a sibling, instructions for a game, revised so the reader understands.
variants.eclectic: Watch for a quick plan before writing, and for sentences changed because they sound better or make more sense to a reader.

watchForNext.neutral: You might hear rhymes and silly sound words being invented, not just repeated, like 'the busy buzzy bee went zoom'. Watch too for a favourite poem said with its rhythm and expression, or a poem made up on the spot.

variants.charlotte_mason: With a poem read each day, watch for favourite lines learned by heart without drilling, and for rhymes of the child's own making.
variants.classical: As poems are memorised and recited, watch for recitation with rhythm and expression, and for new verses invented in the same pattern.
variants.montessori: Watch for rhyming games chosen with friends, and for the sounds of words, rhyme and repeated first sounds, noticed in books and conversation.
variants.waldorf_steiner: Verses and songs fill the day here. Watch for rhythm carried into the child's own speech and play, and for little verses invented for the seasons.
variants.unschooling: Look for wordplay bubbling up everywhere, silly rhymes, made-up songs, puns at dinner, and for favourite poems or songs recited with gusto.
variants.eclectic: Watch for rhymes and sound words invented, not just repeated, and for favourite poems said with their rhythm.
